interest: Japanese radio propaganda tailored differently for Ceylon and India.
overview: This file comprises confidential despatches, intelligence monitoring bulletins, and an interdepartmental routing memorandum from the American Consulate in Colombo, Ceylon, dating from September 1944 to January 1945 and catalogued under State Department decimal file 894.20246C (Japanese military and propaganda activities in Ceylon). The documents detail Japanese radio broadcasts in English and Hindustani originating from Singapore, Saigon, and clandestine stations such as Free Lanka Radio, designed to foment anti-British sentiment across South Asia. U.S. Consuls Max W. Bishop and Robert L. Buell report on how Axis propaganda exploited domestic constitutional unrest in Ceylon—specifically the Ceylon Board of Ministers' boycott of the British Soulbury Commission and speeches by Ceylonese leader D. S. Senanayake—as well as British press controversies regarding American commercial activity in liberated France. Although American consular officials judged the broadcasts largely ineffective among the general Ceylonese public due to the scarcity of shortwave receivers, the reports and intercepts were systematically gathered via the Ceylon Department of Information and Simla monitoring services and disseminated to key U.S. intelligence agencies including the OSS, ONI, MID, and FBI.

subfiles.about: Despatch reporting on confidential British monitoring of Japanese English-language radio propaganda directed at Ceylon.
subfiles.from: Max W. Bishop, American Consul at Colombo, Ceylon
subfiles.summary: Bishop reports regular monitoring of Japanese broadcasts to Ceylon, which resemble those to India but reach few listeners.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 578 from Max W. Bishop on Japanese Propaganda Broadcasts Directed to Ceylon

subfiles.about: Intercepted transcript of a Radio Singapore propaganda commentary urging Ceylon to boycott British constitutional reforms and join Asian liberation efforts.
subfiles.from: Ceylon Department of Information (transmitted by Max W. Bishop)
subfiles.summary: Radio Singapore broadcast of September 4, 1944 by A. Jalalupeen urging Ceylon to boycott the British commission.
subfiles.title: Enclosure to Despatch No. 578: Intercept of Radio Singapore Broadcast by A. Jalalupeen

subfiles.about: Despatch reporting that Japanese radio stations seized on British press reports alleging American exploitation of Paris to produce anti-Allied propaganda.
subfiles.from: Robert L. Buell, American Consul at Colombo, Ceylon
subfiles.summary: Buell reports that Radio Singapore used a Daily Mail story on U.S. exploitation of Paris as propaganda.
subfiles.title: Despatch from Robert L. Buell on Japanese Utilization of Daily Mail Article as Enemy Propaganda

subfiles.about: Despatch transmitting intercepted Japanese broadcasts contrasting Japan's grant of independence to Southeast Asian nations with British rule in Ceylon.
subfiles.from: Robert L. Buell, American Consul at Colombo, Ceylon
subfiles.summary: Buell forwards excerpts of Japanese broadcasts contrasting Burma's 'independence' with Ceylon and linking America to British colonialism.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 608 from Robert L. Buell on Further Japanese Propaganda Broadcasts Directed to Ceylon

subfiles.about: Transcripts of seven enemy radio monitoring bulletins from Saigon, Singapore, and Free Lanka Radio targeting Ceylon and South Asia during September 1944.
subfiles.from: Ceylon Department of Information (transmitted by Robert L. Buell)
subfiles.summary: Summaries of Japanese broadcasts on Ceylon, September 1944, attacking the British reform commission.
subfiles.title: Enclosure to Despatch No. 608: Japanese Broadcasts Referring to Ceylon (September 3–22, 1944)

subfiles.about: Despatch analyzing the tactical differences between Japanese propaganda directed to Ceylon and Japanese broadcasts in Hindustani directed to India.
subfiles.from: Max W. Bishop, American Consul at Colombo, Ceylon
subfiles.summary: Bishop notes that Japanese broadcasts to India treat Ceylon as part of India, unlike those to Ceylon.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 3 from Max W. Bishop on Japanese Propaganda about Ceylon Directed Toward India

subfiles.about: Excerpts from Simla monitoring bulletins containing Hindustani broadcasts attacking the Soulbury Commission and inciting anti-British resistance.
subfiles.from: Simla Monitoring Service (transmitted by Max W. Bishop)
subfiles.summary: Simla monitoring of the 'Soulbury go back' broadcast urging Ceylon's boycott of the reform commission.
subfiles.title: Enclosure to Despatch No. 3: Simla Monitoring Bulletins on the Soulbury Commission and Ceylon

subfiles.about: State Department transmittal slip routing Colombo Despatch No. 3 and its propaganda intercepts to U.S. military and civilian intelligence agencies.
subfiles.summary: State transmittal of Colombo despatch No. 3 to MID, ONI, FBI and OSS.
subfiles.title: State Department Transmittal Memorandum Distributing Colombo Despatch No. 3 to Intelligence Agencies
